title: Calibration by connection count changed delay coverage in 516 selected Allen mouse groups
abstract: We tested timing interval coverage in 1,327 inhibitory connections from 516 inferred mouse groups in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 small data. Across 100 fixed splits of the same cohort, pooled animal-maximum calibration gave median coverage of 94.8%, 88.1%, and 84.9% for animals with 1, 2-3, and at least 4 selected connections. Calibration within these count groups gave medians of 91.1%, 91.6%, and 92.3%. For the largest count group, median mean width rose from 2.007 to 2.352 ms. Neither method reached 90% coverage in every count group in the primary split. The rank guarantee requires exchangeable animal records within count groups, including selection. The repeated splits are not independent tests. Inferred animal IDs, slice selection, small calibration groups, and no external validation limit the result. This is a same-cohort extension of a prior campaign report, not a new statistical method or a biological reliability law. Code, source hashes, derived evidence, and two figures support inspection and reproduction.
